evidence: How the limits were chosen. The same commit was benched against itself (base and head both the same commit, 7 interleaved rounds, medians) in 10 separate jobs on GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 runners (4 vCPU; AMD EPYC 7763, 9V74, 9V45 and an Intel Xeon 6975P-C came up), 2026-11-13. A limit sits above the worst rise of head over base seen in those 10 jobs.

exact, bytes allocated (alloc.*.total-mb): worst rise +0.9% (menu hover 1.17 to 1.19 MB; the bench prints 0.01 MB steps), usually 0.0%. Limit +3% or 0.03 MB. alloc.*.pool-made-mb swings from 0 to 0.4 MB (menu) and 0 to 10 MB (long page) between identical runs, so it is report-only.

exact, hover allocation (hover.*-alloc-mb): printed to 0.1 MB, so one step is up to 11% of a small page; identical runs differ by 0 or one step. Limit +3% or 0.1 MB. hover.*.tiles and hover.*.not-partial were identical in all 10 jobs: any rise fails.
exact, scroll notch (tile.*.maps, repoints, packets, raw-kb, deflated-kb): identical in all 10 jobs. Limit +1% or the 0.1 step of the printed number (0.15).

timing, gated: worst rise of head over base in the 10 jobs (limit): tile.*.cpu-ms and canvas-ms +2.2% (10%); hover market repaint-cpu +3.6%, ahead-cpu +3.3% (15%); hover menu ahead-cpu +5.3% (15%); hover menu repaint-cpu +9.4% (20%); render menu full +4.5%, draw +1.9%, hover +3.8% (15%); render market full +5.2% (15%); render landing full +6.5% (15%). All of them also keep an absolute floor in ms so that a 0.1 ms step of the printed number is never a failure.

timing, report-only, too noisy on hosted runners to gate at 15%: render.pages/market.draw-ms (+10.4%), render.pages/market.hover-ms (+16.7%), render.*.hover-draw-ms (+9.1%, values under 1.5 ms), render.samples/landing.draw-ms (+10.0%), every hover.*.layout-cpu-ms (+9.3% menu; about 3 ms), and every timing of the shop page (+17% hover repaint, +15% layout; about 10 ms, bimodal from run to run). A first draft also benched render shop and radial-clip: +42% and +36% between identical jobs, so they were dropped. Every timing metric not named in a rule above falls to the last rule and is report-only.

Timing that goes over a limit is measured again (3 more rounds of that bench) before it fails, so one noisy neighbour cannot fail a PR; a real slowdown is still there. Exact metrics are not measured again.
To change a limit, edit this file in the PR that needs it: the change is reviewed with the PR. There is no label or comment that overrides the gate.
